title: Warm-Starting MaxCut Relaxation via Low-Depth Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Bao G. Bach, Ilya Safro, Filip B. Maciejewski
abstract: Quantum optimization has attracted growing interest as quantum hardware continues to improve, yet state-of-the-art classical solvers remain a formidable benchmark for practical utility. Rather than seeking a fully quantum replacement for classical optimization, we propose a hybrid strategy that uses quantum information to enhance leading classical heuristics. Specifically, we introduce a warm-start method based on local correlators obtained from the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), and use this information to initialize the Burer-Monteiro (BM) rank-two relaxation. We demonstrate numerically that, compared to a random, multi-start initialization baseline (a standard strategy used for BM), this quantum-informed initialization offers a significant head start, i.e., high-quality solutions with very small number of iterations, for two problem classes -- random Erdős Rényi graphs with edge density of $10\%$ (ER-10) and fully-connected Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass models, at $n=500$ and $n=1000$ qubits. At the same time, given enough iterations, the random baseline often eventually catches up and slightly outperforms the warm-start strategy on average, an effect visibly stronger for $n=500$ than for $n=1000$. The results demonstrate an exploitation/exploration tradeoff of using WS to quickly arrive at very good solutions vs exploring slightly better solutions with a larger iterations budget via a standard strategy. Our results highlight how low-depth quantum circuits can provide useful structural information for classical optimization and suggest a promising route toward near-term quantum utility through quantum-assisted initialization.
summary: This work proposes using local correlators from the QAOA algorithm to 'warm-start' the Burer-Monteiro relaxation for solving the MaxCut problem. The results show this quantum-informed initialization provides a significant speedup, quickly reaching high-quality solutions compared to random starts. However, it highlights an exploitation/exploration tradeoff, suggesting that while quantum assistance is useful for rapid initial progress, exhaustive classical search might still yield marginally better final results.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve classical optimization heuristics for the MaxCut problem by incorporating structural information derived from quantum computation.
main_result: A warm-start initialization using QAOA local correlators provides a significant early advantage in finding high-quality solutions quickly, though random multi-start methods can eventually surpass it with sufficient computational budget.
method: The authors propose a hybrid strategy where low-depth QAOA outputs (local correlators $\langle Z_i Z_j angle$) are used to initialize the Burer-Monteiro rank-two relaxation solver for MaxCut, which is then compared against random initialization strategies.
model_or_system: The problem studied is the weighted MAXCUT problem on a graph $G(V, E)$, formulated as an Ising model ($\mathcal{H}_C$). Benchmarks include random Erdős–Rényi (ER-10) graphs and Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass models.
key_observables: Best found energy, paired difference in best energy vs. baseline, WinRate (probability of matching or exceeding baseline performance).
important_parameters: Graph size ($n=500$ and $n=1000$), QAOA depth parameter ($p=1$).
main_assumptions: The comparison is limited to the BM refinement stage, not an end-to-end quantum advantage; the warm-start relies on mapping low-depth correlators to initial parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 2 shows performance vs. iteration budget for ER-10 graphs ($n=500, 1000$), illustrating WS's early lead and MultiStart's eventual crossover. Figure 3 presents similar results for the SK model.
paper_structure: The paper details deriving QAOA correlators to initialize BM relaxation, compares this warm-start approach against random multi-starts on ER and SK ensembles across varying iteration budgets, and analyzes the resulting exploitation/exploration tradeoff.
why_interesting: It demonstrates a concrete pathway for near-term quantum utility by showing how limited quantum circuit outputs can provide valuable structural guidance to classical optimization solvers tackling hard combinatorial problems like MaxCut.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Warm Start Framework for Burer-Monteiro rank-two relaxation using QAOA correlators ⟨ZiZj⟩. The corresponding marginal distributions of the probability of edge (i, j) being cut are then mapped via a Goemans-Williamson-inspired trigonometric function to ˜Q. We then find the closest rank-2 correlation matrix via projecting onto the two largest positive eigenvalues of ˜Q, followed by least-squares error optimization. The resulting matrix is then interpreted as encoding the angles θ that are used as the initial point for Burer-Monteiro rank-two relaxation.
